title: IV / Adversarial Review — Independent Verification of Sprint Claims
methodology: Each major sprint claim is examined adversarially: what could go wrong, what is unverified, what contradictions remain

claims_reviewed.claim: 42/42 examples produce real API output (no-ops eliminated)
verification_basis: per-example-output-proof.json: 9 repaired examples have stdout proof
template_first validator: runs _validate_code() before returning template — malformed templates fail generation
adversarial_questions: Q: Are the 33 non-repaired examples (from prior sprints) still valid?
A: Yes — they were validated in the durable-full-closure sprint (42/42 fresh generation+build+run); this sprint's E2E re-ran all 42
Q: Could the dotnet run stdout be captured from a different run than the current code?
A: The proof captures stdout post-repair; example IDs match; risk is LOW

claims_reviewed.claim: All 6 families have publication packages (diagram/slides/email newly created)
adversarial_questions: Q: Were the new packages actually built with dotnet build (not just created structurally)?
A: Yes — build_verified=true in report; packages have proper .csproj, Directory.Packages.props, global.json
Q: Are the example Program.cs files in the packages the same as the validated examples?
A: The packages reference examples in workspace/verification/latest/families/ — same source as E2E validation

claims_reviewed.claim: Reviewer status is honest (NOT_REVIEWED, not fabricated PASS)
verification_basis: per_family: cells and pdf mark require_example_reviewer=true but reviewer_available=false
deterministic checks confirmed PASS for all 42 examples
adversarial_questions: Q: Does NOT_REVIEWED mean quality is unverified?
A: No — deterministic _validate_code() + _validate_code_from_constraints() run for all 42; these check REQUIRED/FORBIDDEN patterns, which are meaningful structural checks
Q: Could template_first bypass the reviewer's quality checks?
A: Templates are validated by the same _validate_code() call before returning; a template that fails structural checks causes generation to fail
claims_reviewed.residual_risk: MEDIUM — LLM-based semantic review would provide higher confidence, but deterministic checks catch the most common failure modes

verification_basis: validation-truth-model.json: 42 validated (all build+run), 41 PR candidates (words-comparer excluded by advisory), words package = 7 PR candidates
adversarial_questions: Q: Is the words-comparer exclusion correct or artificially reducing the count?

A: same_format_converter_guard is an advisory (not blocking); words-comparer IS validated and passes build+run; exclusion is debatable (see K3 work-ahead). The exclusion is conservative and documented.
Q: Why does the truth model say '8 words in old package' but the package has 7?
A: Old package was created before the advisory exclusion; current package has 7. Truth model documents both states.
claims_reviewed.residual_risk: LOW — advisory exclusion is documented and debatable but not contradictory

claims_reviewed.claim: Validator count increased from 145 to 147 (2 new rules added)
verification_basis: 9/9 new rule tests pass in test_evidence_validator.py
full pytest running to confirm no regressions
adversarial_questions: Q: Do the new rules actually enforce the sprint's quality claims, or are they trivially bypassed?

A: Rule 146 requires still_no_op=0 when repaired examples exist — cannot be bypassed without a real output proof. Rule 147 requires all 6 family names in the package report — cannot be bypassed without the correct structure.
Q: Are the new rules only applicable to bundles that explicitly include these reports?
A: Correct — both rules are gated on file presence (not-applicable if files missing). This is by design: prior sprints that predate these reports should not fail retroactively.

claims_reviewed.claim: Prior Pass 3 ZIP entry count (549) is correct
verification_basis: integrity-protocol.json: 549 = 545 tracked + 4 metadata; 547 would have been before zip-file-list.txt added to metadata
Prior reviewer complaint (549 vs 547) explained: reviewer saw intermediate state
adversarial_questions: Q: Can this be verified without re-extracting the ZIP?
A: The ZIP was built in a prior sprint; the zip-file-list.txt inside the ZIP should contain the entry list. Without re-reading the ZIP, this is a documented reconciliation only.
Q: Is there a risk that the count is still wrong?
A: The protocol documents the build process (script creates zip-file-list.txt AFTER ZIP is built); the inconsistency is structural, not numerical. 549 is the final agreed count.
claims_reviewed.residual_risk: LOW — historical artifact count; does not affect current sprint quality
